deviations_from_card: Two commits instead of three: the test commit (red by design, e4f3c8df, cases 13-17 red and 18 guard; the repo gate was not run on it) and one refactor commit (ec77ba14) holding both the call core move and the per-provider abort handling, since splitting the shared hunks of the same files was not worth a partial-hunk commit. Case 18's two deadlineMs asserts (codexCli.deadlineMs 240000, claudeCli.deadlineMs undefined) were moved into case 16, because they cannot be green before the property exists; case 18 is a true guard (a prompt stub resolves with provider and numeric ms for all five kinds) and was green before. shape.answer keeps its (provider, req) argument order with the kind as an optional third parameter defaulting to 'text', instead of a leading kind, because tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs, uat-recertify-test.cjs and uat-verdict-test.cjs (outside the write set) call shape.answer(p, req). listen() gained an optional third parameter { timeoutMs } to carry the deadline, since it takes positional arguments rather than a ListenRequest.
notes: User-visible or operator-visible behaviour changes the card did not list: (1) vision now has a 180 s deadline, embed 60 s, speak 30 s where there was none; the embed 60 s default applies to the whole lesson-window batch in lib/library/lessons.ts:36 on a cold Ollama model load, so a very first retrieval on a large transcript may now fail with a timeout (lessons then fall back as on any embed failure) where it used to wait; raise DEADLINE_MS.embed or pass timeoutMs there if that bites. (2) The timeout message is now 'The <kind> engine took too long. Please retry.' for every kind (text was 'The text engine ...', same wording). (3) Piper spawn failure is now an EngineError 'unreachable' ('piper could not start: ...') and a non-zero exit an EngineError 'exit', instead of raw Errors; the other raw throws (res.json(), readFileSync, readFile of last.txt) are typed by the core as 'exit' with the first line of their message, not wrapped individually. (4) When the deadline passes, the claude, codex and Piper children are killed on the signal and the Ollama, ElevenLabs and listen fetches are aborted; the core rejects first, so the error kind is always 'timeout' with the provider's registry name (e.g. 'claude-cli', not 'claude-cli/haiku'; the old text timeout carried the reported model string, the new one carries p.name), which no caller reads. (5) A provider that wraps run(req) and drops the second argument (lab-bench, calc-model-yield) still gets the deadline from the core. Disagreement with the scout: none on design. No TV screen was touched; no TV capture ran, none needed. No live model call ran; every case stubs the provider seam. Kotlin gate not applicable (no tv-app change). The shared surface lock was not needed: desk/package.json was not edited (the cases extend the already-wired engines-rules-test.cjs).
